pool.text: Great Fire destroyed about a quarter of the inner city
Major cholera outbreak badly handled by city government
Hamburg City Hall completed as Neo‑Renaissance building
Tierpark Hagenbeck zoo founded with moated, barless enclosures
Hamburg Airport established, becoming Germany's fifth biggest airport
Chilehaus built, brick expressionist office building shaped like an ocean liner
Hamburg became a Gau within Nazi Germany's administrative division
Allied fire‑bombing created firestorm destroying several boroughs
Hamburg surrendered to British forces three days after Hitler's death
North Sea flood inundated one‑fifth of Hamburg, killing over 300 people
English Theatre of Hamburg founded, oldest professional English‑language theatre in Germany
German premiere of Cats sparked continuous musical productions in the city
German reunification opened new ambitions for the Port of Hamburg
Construction began on the HafenCity urban development project
More than 2,500 Stolpersteine installed honoring deported citizens
Olaf Scholz became mayor of Hamburg on 7 March
Speicherstadt and Kontorhausviertel designated UNESCO World Heritage Sites
Elbphilharmonie opened, sail‑shaped concert hall atop old warehouse
G20 summit protests clashed with police around Sternschanze and Rote Flora
Law passed to phase out coal‑based thermal and electric energy production
